authentication: oidc: bearer tokens of issuer https://login.fleet.example/ for audience 'fleet-api', algorithms RS256 only (HS*/none refused), signature verified against the JWKS at https://login.fleet.example/.well-known/jwks.json (TLS verified, private CA only added through oidc_ca_bundle, response capped, cached 300 s, one fetch attempt per 30 s, stale keys served for at most oidc_jwks_stale_max_s), exp/nbf/iat required with 30 s leeway; provider unreachable, failing or unusable is 503, not 401; the client is verified against a local HTTPS provider in tests/test_jwks.py
execution: generated tests run only through the v1.9 trust model, in a copy of the project; the local executor is process hygiene, not a sandbox

multi_tenant.principal_tenant_binding: enforced: the tenant path parameter must equal the verified fleet_id claim of the token, otherwise 403; a token without a valid tenant claim is 401

rls.context_scope: transaction (set_config third argument true); never SET at session level
rls.context_set_by: get_tenant_session, from the authenticated principal's tenant, before the first statement of the request transaction
rls.context_trust: any statement run as the application role within that transaction can change it: the boundary holds against missing filters and ordinary application bugs, not against SQL injection or arbitrary SQL as that role
rls.owner: migrations run as the owner; FORCE makes the owner subject to the policies too unless it is a superuser or BYPASSRLS
rls.role_privileges: SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on the tenant tables and USAGE on the schema; no DDL, no TRUNCATE, no BYPASSRLS, no CREATEROLE, no access to alembic_version or pg_authid

storage_isolation: tenant_id column on every entity and a tenant filter on every repository query
composite foreign keys (tenant_id, id) between tenant tables: a row cannot reference another tenant's row

row-level security: ENABLE + FORCE on every tenant table, policy USING/WITH CHECK on fleet.current (NULL context: no row visible or writable), application role fleet_api without BYPASSRLS (GRANT SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE only), tenant context set with set_config(..., true) at the start of the request transaction, migrations run by the owner

not_claimed: network or filesystem isolation of executed tests
protection against code the generated tests execute (the trust model is process hygiene, not a sandbox)

isolation against SQL statements executed as the application role (an injection that reaches statement level can change the tenant context; the policies protect against missing filters, not against arbitrary SQL)
business rules beyond the declared policy (roles per operation and ownership are enforced; anything finer is the author's code)
validation against a real identity provider (the JWKS client is verified against a local HTTPS provider with a private CA; a provider's own behaviour is not)
OAuth2 authorization flows (code, PKCE, device), consent, token issuance, refresh tokens or an authorization server (only externally issued tokens are validated)
public resources inside an authenticated API
authorization proven by the name of a dependency (the auditor counts a policy only where its code shows the decision)

persistence.infrastructure_failure: database unreachable is answered 503 (problem+json), distinct from 401/403/404
persistence.migrations: alembic: generated environment and initial migration; tables are created only by `alembic upgrade head`

resource_authorization: roles: per-operation roles checked in a route dependency before the service runs (403): create needs dispatcher
